body.statement:
With only snapshots \(k=0,1,2\), if \(p\ge3\) and \(d_0
e0\), every admissible explanation lies in a local fiber of dimension \((p-1)(p-2)/2\). With four snapshots, \(\det K_0
e0\) implies the rational recovery identity \(V=K_1K_0^{-1}\); the condition \(\det K_0
e0\) holds outside a proper algebraic subset of the admissible parameter domain. Thus three snapshots are generically locally nonidentifying for \(p\ge3\), whereas four snapshots generically identify \(V\) and the full explanation whenever the unique recovered candidate passes the admissibility filters.
body.proof_tex:
The exact three-snapshot compatibility certificate, torsor classification, local dimensions, zero-displacement elbow, and supermodel transfer are established by \(\text{thm:three-snapshot-exact-classification}\).  In particular, if \(d_0\ne0\), then \(r=1\) and every local admissible branch has dimension
\[
 \frac{(p-1)(p-2)}2,
\]
which is positive for \(p\ge3\).  At a true structural explanation, \(\text{ass:linear-flow}\) gives
\[
 d_0=(V-I_p)(\mu_0-x^\star).
\]
By \(\text{ass:hurwitz}\) and \(\text{ass:spacing}\), \(\rho(V)<1\), so \(I_p-V\) is invertible.  Hence \(d_0=0\) is exactly the proper affine locus \(\mu_0=x^\star\); its complement is open and dense in the mean parameter.  This proves the generic three-snapshot assertion.

We prove the four-snapshot assertion directly from the observable equations.  By \(\text{ass:strict-decrease}\), \(H_0,H_1,H_2\) are positive definite and therefore invertible.  If \(W\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{raw}}\), then \(WH_0W^{\mathsf T}=H_1\succ0\) implies \(\operatorname{rank}(W)=p\), so \(W\) is invertible.  Using the two covariance congruences in \(\text{def:raw-fiber}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 M_1W
 &=H_2H_1^{-1}W\\
 &=(WH_1W^{\mathsf T})(WH_0W^{\mathsf T})^{-1}W\\
 &=WH_1W^{\mathsf T}W^{-\mathsf T}H_0^{-1}W^{-1}W\\
 &=WH_1H_0^{-1}=WM_0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The first mean equation in \(\text{def:raw-fiber}\) is \(d_1=Wd_0\).  The intertwining identity therefore gives, by induction on \(j\),
\[
 M_1^jd_1=M_1^jWd_0=WM_0^jd_0
 \qquad(0\le j<p).
\]
Taking these vectors as columns yields
\[
 K_1=WK_0.
\]
Consequently, on the cyclic chart \(\det K_0\ne0\), every raw candidate is the observable rational functional
\[
 W=K_1K_0^{-1}=\mathcal K((m_k),(C_k)).
\]
In particular, the structural transition satisfies \(V=K_1K_0^{-1}\), and there is at most one raw, hence at most one admissible, transition.  This proves equality between the causal target and the observable recovery map rather than defining the target by that map.

It remains to prove that the cyclic chart is generic.  Choose pairwise distinct numbers \(v_i\in(0,1)\), and set
\[
 V=\operatorname{diag}(v_1,\ldots,v_p),\qquad
 G=h^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\log v_1,\ldots,\log v_p),\qquad
 \Sigma=I_p,\qquad E=I_p.
\]
Choose \(u=\mu_0-x^\star\) with every coordinate nonzero.  The generator is real, Hurwitz, and in the principal alias strip, while \(V=\exp(hG)\).  The latent covariance at snapshot \(j\) is \(\operatorname{diag}(v_i^{2j})\), so common-noise cancellation gives
\[
 H_j=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(v_i^{2j}(1-v_i^2)\bigr)\succ0
 \qquad(j=0,1,2),
\]
and
\[
 M_0=H_1H_0^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(v_1^2,\ldots,v_p^2).
\]
The affine mean recursion gives \(d_0=(V-I_p)u\), whose coordinates are all nonzero.  The \(i\)-th row of \(K_0\) is
\[
 d_{0i}(1,v_i^2,\ldots,v_i^{2(p-1)}).
\]
Subtracting successive columns in the usual determinant recursion for this Vandermonde matrix gives
\[
 \det K_0
 =\left(\prod_{i=1}^p d_{0i}\right)
 \prod_{1\le i<j\le p}(v_j^2-v_i^2)\ne0.
\]
The example has \(E=I_p\succ0\), so it lies in the strict admissible parameter domain.

Parameterize that domain by the transition coordinates \((V,\Sigma,E,x^\star,\mu_0)\).  The entries of \(H_j\) and \(d_j\) are polynomial in these coordinates, whereas the entries of \(M_0=H_1H_0^{-1}\) are rational with denominator a power of \(\det H_0\).  Thus \(\det K_0\) is rational on \(\det H_0\ne0\).  Clearing the denominator gives a polynomial numerator.  The preceding admissible example makes this numerator nonzero, so it is not the zero polynomial.  Its zero set is therefore a proper algebraic subset.  For completeness, the zero set of a nonzero real polynomial has empty interior and Lebesgue measure zero: induction on the number of coordinates reduces the assertion to the finite-root property of a nonzero univariate polynomial outside the common zero set of its coefficient polynomials.  Hence \(\det K_0\ne0\) outside a proper algebraic subset of the admissible transition-coordinate domain.

On this complement, the rational map recovers the sole raw candidate.  If that candidate passes the stability, logarithm-cut, Stein, and recovered-noise positivity filters in \(\text{def:admissible-fiber}\), then \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\) is its singleton.  The bijection in \(\text{thm:admissible-fiber}\) then identifies \(G\), the latent initial covariance, the common measurement covariance, the equilibrium, and \(\mu_0=m_0\).  If the candidate fails a filter, there is no admissible explanation.  This proves the four-snapshot generic-identification claim.
body.justification: The exact three-snapshot norm certificate and stabilizer dimension isolate the fourth destructive snapshot as the generic identification resource created by unknown common measurement covariance.
body.gap: Known-state-covariance results do not cover the shared unknown additive covariance: after differencing, three-snapshot compatibility leaves an \(O(p-1)\) fiber generically and an \(O(p)\) fiber at zero mean displacement, while the fourth snapshot supplies the second congruence needed by the rational Krylov map.
body.consumer: Experimental designers obtain an observable population certificate for three-snapshot compatibility and a sharp reason to collect a fourth destructive snapshot when a common covariance calibration sample is unavailable.
